Every Thursday, but only during June, July, and August, forever (to 1999)
Every Friday the 13th, forever (to 2000)
cases.note: The RFC's example also has EXDATE;TZID=America/New_York:19970902T090000, which takes the unsynchronized DTSTART out; a rule fixture has no EXDATE, so the first occurrence stays and the RFC's list follows it. Erratum 5920 (rejected) asked to move DTSTART onto 13 February 1998.
cases.divergence: DTSTART isn't a date the rule produces. The first occurrence is always one, and counts toward COUNT as RFC 5545 §3.3.10 says, even when the rule wouldn't produce it or UNTIL is earlier. RFC 5545 leaves that set undefined and python-dateutil leaves DTSTART out; we keep it because the application's event exists at that time (ADR 0048 point 4).
cases.secondOracleNote: ical.js leaves out DTSTART when the rule doesn't produce it or UNTIL is earlier, as python-dateutil does.
